title: Solar panel incentives for private buildings and the Electric Vehicle Early Adoption Incentive
asked: Three MPs asked about the policy basis for subsidising electric vehicle purchases but not residential rooftop solar, the take-up of both, the barriers to solar installation in private residential and commercial buildings including MCST-managed ones, and whether grants, tax reliefs, mandates or other measures will be introduced.
asked_by: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat, Dr Choo Pei Ling and Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
response: Ms Gan Siow Huang said Singapore has reached two gigawatt-peak of installed solar capacity and targets three gigawatt-peak by 2030, with private residential buildings having solar panels rising from about 1,400 in 2020 to about 6,900 in 2025, or about 8% of all private residential buildings. Eligible private buildings can tap the Green Mark Incentive Scheme for Existing Buildings 2.0 for grant support of up to 50% of energy improvement works, capped at $1.2 million, and there are no plans at this stage to mandate solar installation on buildings. The Electric Vehicle Early Adoption Incentive, implemented in January 2021, has benefited more than 55,000 electric cars and taxis as of March 2026 and will cease from 1 January 2027. She said the Government will monitor adoption rates and is prepared to consider additional measures if necessary.

key_points.point: Singapore has reached two gigawatt-peak of installed solar capacity, with a target of three gigawatt-peak by 2030
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: We have achieved two gigawatt-peak of installed solar capacity island-wide and have set an increased target of three gigawatt-peak by 2030.

key_points.point: Private residential buildings with solar panels rose from around 1,400 in 2020 to around 6,900 in 2025, about 8% of all private residential buildings
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: from around 1,400 in 2020 to around 6,900 in 2025

key_points.point: The payback period for rooftop solar can be five years or less
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: the payback period for rooftop solar can be five years or even less

key_points.point: Eligible private buildings can get grant support of up to 50% of energy improvement works under the Green Mark Incentive Scheme for Existing Buildings 2.0, capped at $1.2 million
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: eligible building owners can benefit from grant support of up to 50% of the cost of their energy improvement works, capped at $1.2 million

key_points.point: There are no plans at this stage to mandate solar panel installation on buildings
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: we have no plans at this stage to mandate solar panel installation on buildings

key_points.point: The Electric Vehicle Early Adoption Incentive was implemented in January 2021 and will cease from 1 January 2027
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: The EEAI was implemented in January 2021

key_points.point: As of March 2026, more than 55,000 electric cars and taxis have benefited from the EEAI
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: As of March 2026, more than 55,000 electric cars and taxis have benefited from the EEAI.

key_points.point: Building owners have raised concerns about roof waterproofing integrity and vendor reliability, and some prefer to keep rooftops for other uses
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: some are concerned about whether it will affect the integrity of the waterproofing for the roof

key_points.point: New buildings must meet BCA's Code for Environmental Sustainability of Buildings, with solar recognised as an acceptable carbon-reduction measure
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: New buildings are required to meet standards under the Building and Construction Authority's (BCA's) Code for Environmental Sustainability of Buildings

key_points.point: Simplified fire safety requirements exempt more than half of solar panel installations on metal-roofed buildings, saving eligible business owners up to 30% on total construction costs
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: The simplified fire safety requirements exempt more than half of all solar panel installations on metal-roofed buildings

key_points.point: SkillsFuture Singapore has partnered Sembcorp Solar as a SkillsFuture Queen Bee since 2024 to train workers in the sector
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: SkillsFuture Singapore also partners Sembcorp Solar as a SkillsFuture Queen Bee since 2024

key_points.point: BCA's review of the Building Strata Management Act includes a proposal to lower the resolution requirement for third-party solar ownership models from 75% to possibly 50%
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: They are exploring a reduction from 75% to possibly 50%.

key_points.point: The suggestion of a starter kit for private property owners will be seriously considered
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang

left_open: Whether comparable capital grants or property tax rebates will be introduced for residential solar panels
The take-up rate of the EEAI expressed as a rate, rather than a number of vehicles
Whether solar installation will be mandated for all new buildings and estates
Whether greater incentives will be provided for existing building owners to install solar panels
Whether a white list of solar vendors will be provided for private property owners
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered the economics of solar adoption, MCST approval thresholds, solar-ready building design, agency coordination and workforce development.
